run_location: prod-box in-container (i-04b155fafcc90042b), user standing campaign approval
purpose: Out-of-sample CONFIRMATORY test of the exploratory v3 subset finding (substantive-deliberative class scored 7/10=0.70 in-sample). All 14 scored cases are FRESH (none in the v2.1/v3 sets) and all substantive-deliberative. The set is deliberately CONTROL-HEAVY (8 control-won / 6 treatment-won) to power the primary endpoint.

audit.auditor_blind_guess_accuracy: 6/14 = 0.429 (below chance) -> wording does not leak winners
audit.auditor_control_won_recall: 2/8 (auditor made the same pro-change error -> cases are hard the right way)

config.engine: live SimulationRunner (blinded control-vs-treatment stimulus, generic conversion elicitation, direction-only scoring)

baselines_to_beat.always_control: 8/14 = 0.571 (the strongest constant baseline on this control-heavy set; headline must beat THIS, not just 0.5)

PRIMARY_endpoint.name: control-class accuracy = (# of the 8 control-won cases the sim predicts control) / 8
PRIMARY_endpoint.rationale: Balance-independent; directly measures whether the sim RESISTS its measured pro-change tilt on FRESH adverse-signal cases. Headline-significance is underpowered at any feasible n, so this is the decisive read.

decision_rule.supports_narrow_positive: control-class >= 0.5 (>=4/8) -> the sim shows balanced discrimination on fresh out-of-sample control-won cases -> escalate toward the narrow sellable claim (substantive deliberative product-change direction), expand for significance.
decision_rule.confirms_intrinsic_tilt: control-class <= 3/8 -> pro-change tilt is intrinsic, not a v3 artifact -> the in-scope 'positive' was treatment-lean flattering -> honest bounded-null; the lever is #221 (de-bias the pro-change prior at outcome elicitation).
decision_rule.void: if null-integrity cert VOIDs, report VOID.

prediction_of_record.PRIMARY_control_class: I predict the tilt LARGELY PERSISTS: control-class ~2-3/8 (0.25-0.375), i.e. BELOW the 0.5 balanced-discrimination bar. These are adverse-signal / second-order cases (reference-price reset, choice overload, adverse quality signal, engagement-revenue divergence, ad mistiming) where a naive 'would users like this feature?' simulation predicts the feature helps -> treatment -> WRONG. The independent auditor's blind 2/8 on these same cases supports this.
prediction_of_record.treatment_class: ~5-6/6 (the sim stays good when the change genuinely wins) -> the asymmetry (high treatment-class, low control-class) IS the pro-change tilt made visible.
prediction_of_record.headline_dir_acc: ~0.50-0.57 (driven by high treatment-class + low control-class), roughly TIES the always-control baseline -> NOT a certified positive on the headline. The informative content is the per-class STRUCTURE, not the headline.
prediction_of_record.what_would_surprise_me: control-class >= 4/8 would be a genuine, un-predicted positive -> strong evidence the sim can resist its tilt and reason about adverse-signal cases -> the first credible fresh-data narrow positive.

honesty_notes: This prediction is deliberately un-flattering to the product (I expect it to fail the primary). A locked prediction that turns out wrong in the FLATTERING direction (control-class surprisingly high) would therefore be strong, credible positive evidence.

Control-heavy by design: real control-won product-change cases are scarce (publication bias); 8 is near the obtainable ceiling from primary sources. n=8 control-won is decisive for the tilt question (0-2/8 = tilt; >=4/8 = resistance) even though the headline is underpowered.
Memorization control: the famous jam study and a near-null Bing case are HELD OUT (not scored) so recitation cannot inflate control-class.
Treatment-won half includes 2 vendor-sourced directional cases (bionicgloves, blivakker) flagged lower-credibility; they only affect the secondary treatment-class, not the primary.
